title: Top-Customer Signals and Dynamic Roadmap Trigger Matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create and operationalize a dynamic roadmap trigger matrix that converts high-signal customer events into prioritized roadmap actions and gating rules. Matrix will combine quantitative signals (MRR at risk, API error spike, request volume growth) and qualitative signals (C-suite escalations, regulatory asks) to produce an inferred priority score and recommended response: A) immediate P0 triage, B) prioritized planning slot, C) monitor/engage. Goal: reduce time-to-decision for top-account asks, improve consistency of trade-offs, and create auditable routing into product planning lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Schema and scoring weights documented in Confluence and agreed by GTM/CS/Eng
Automation prototype that maps three real signals to Linear tickets + Slack alerts (sandbox environment)
Playbook for human gating and review defined and sign-offs obtained from Head of CS and Head of Eng
Dashboards showing historical signal->decision mapping and precision/recall over past 12 months
Pilot with 6 top accounts for one cycle and retro showing time-to-decision improvement
proposed_scoring_model: MRR exposure: 0-40 points (tiered by ARR bracket)
Escalation severity: 0-30 points (1=ops question, 5=legal/regulatory or executive escalation)
Integration depth: 0-15 points (single call vs platform integration)
Strategic alignment / OKR fit: 0-15 points (mapped to product OKRs)
Score buckets: 70+ => P0 Triage; 40-69 => Planning Slot; <40 => Monitor/Customer Success action

risks_and_tradeoffs: False positives from noisy telemetry could cause unnecessary escalations; mitigation: require two independent signals or manual gate for scores 70-79
Over-automation may reduce relationship-driven nuance for strategic customers; mitigation: include an override by assigned AM with justification logged
Tightly coupling to OKRs may bias toward short-term wins; mitigation: include strategic alignment as only 15/100 points and require product sponsor for long-term projects
Dependency on data quality (billing/MRR feeds) – data pipeline owners must provide SLA for sync latency
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize scoring schema and thresholds; Confluence approval

Week 5: Human gating UI in internal console and ops playbook
Week 6: Pilot with six accounts, collect metrics, and retro
metrics_for_success: Mean time from customer signal to product decision (target: <48 hours for P0 cases)
Precision of automated P0 decisions (target: >= 85% in pilot)
Number of top-account requests processed via the matrix vs ad-hoc (target: 60% adoption after pilot)
Customer satisfaction for pilot accounts (NPS/CSAT follow-up >= previous quarter)
